title: Sukkah 3b — Practice Quiz
source: Questions and correct answers taken directly from the Dafyomi Advancement Forum quiz for Sukkah 3 (dafyomi.co.il/sukah/quiz/su-qz-003.htm), questions 3–6.

questions.q: A house that doesn't have an area of 4×4 amos is exempt from...
options: The special sale rules for walled-city houses
questions.explain: All of these halachot are tied to verses that specifically say "house" — so none apply to a structure too small to legally count as one.

questions.q: A house that doesn't have an area of 4×4 amos can still be used for __________.
questions.explain: It can't hold the food for eiruvei chatzeirot — not fit for residence. But it can hold the food for shittufei mevoyos (merging an alleyway), since for that purpose it's no worse than an ordinary open courtyard.

questions.q: One partner may force the other to divide a 4×7 house.
options: True — as long as it starts out 4×4
questions.explain: The Gemara reattributes this: such a structure doesn't have the din of division like a courtyard at all. Courtyard division runs on separate mechanics (Rav Huna: by entrance ratio; Rav Chisda: 4 amos flat per entrance, then split the rest) — not a simple forced division.

questions.q: Partners are dividing a courtyard. Reuven has 3 entrances, Shimon has 2 — how much of the courtyard does Reuven get?
options: Each takes a 4×4 entrance and divides the balance
questions.explain: Rav Huna divides purely by entrance ratio (3:2 → 60%, option B). Rav Chisda gives each entrance a flat 4 amos first, then splits the remainder evenly (option C). The real answer is that it's disputed between those two mechanisms.
